## A. Decisions needed before Wednesday

**A1. Errata to my judicial affidavit.** Two clerical errors (Part B1). Do you want the attached Manifestation (Annex 1) filed and served before the hearing, or should I state the corrections under oath when I affirm the affidavit? I would rather we correct them than have Atty. Ramos raise them on cross.

**A2. Which theory leads.** My affidavit says in two places that the SPA was "limited to the negotiation of the sale which does not include the power to sell" (Q26, Q53). The certified copy of the SPA also authorizes Cesar "to sign and execute the necessary documents … as well as to receive the proceeds of the aforementioned sale." My prepared position is the **class limitation**: whatever Cesar could do, he could do it only "in favor of third persons in possession of CONTRACTS TO SELL executed by the previous administrator, MR. BEN LLAMANZARES … after prior consultation with us." Mrs. Balane was never in that class and the owners were never consulted. **Which theory does your brief argue?** If I am shown Q53 on cross, should I concede the wording and rest on the class, or defend "no power to sell"? I will hold to whichever you choose.

**A3. Gloria Balane's judicial affidavit.** Has the court ruled on their motion to admit it (their Manifestation of 19 May 2026)? If it remains excluded, I will not refer to anything in it. If it has been admitted, I would like to use her admissions (rent to the owners' side; entry through Kenneth Asistin; no contact with the Keesey owners before buying).

**A4. Supplemental judicial affidavit.** Several helpful facts are not in my affidavit (Part C6 and Annex 2). Will you seek leave to file a short supplemental affidavit, or hold these for re-direct and rebuttal? I understand the five-day period has passed and leave would be needed.

**A5. Documents I do not have.** (a) The 4 September 2026 order that cancelled the 9 September and 7 October settings; I know the new dates only as relayed. (b) Any ruling on our Motion for Summary Judgment (24 April 2026). (c) Whether a Reply to their Comment-Opposition was finally filed (my copy is marked draft, 11 May 2026). (d) The certified filed copy of the Complaint. (e) The RTC Branch 41 record of Cesar's petition for a new owner's duplicate (order of 30 January 2017): which title or titles it covered, what Cesar alleged, and whether the co-owners were notified. (f) The Registry's 2021 registration file for the sale: who presented the instruments and surrendered the replacement duplicate. Could your office send every order within a day of receipt from now on?

**A6. The 2017 partition as a second ground (Part C8).** Mrs. Balane's title was issued on a Partition-Subdivision Agreement dated 15 March 2017 that split T-52540 into her lot and ours. No one on our side signed it or knew of it, and neither SPA gave Cesar any power to partition. Would you plead, in the alternative, that TCT No. 079-2021002126 must be cancelled because no valid partition ever separated a specific lot from the co-ownership, whatever the court decides about the deed? And will you issue a subpoena duces tecum to the Registry for the complete file of Entry No. 2021003236, including the agreement itself, and to the Clerk of Court for Atty. Donald E. Asis's notarial registers for 2016 and 2017? I will file the Registry request for certified copies this week in any case.

**A7. Their "builders in good faith" defense (Part C10).** Their twelfth defense and counterclaim ask for reimbursement of the price, taxes, registration and survey expenses and "the value of necessary and useful improvements, with the corresponding right of retention." If we win on title and lose on this, they stay until paid. Would you (a) answer it in the memorandum period by period, as set out in C10; (b) issue subpoenas duces tecum now to the Office of the Building Official (permits, applications and certificates of occupancy for every structure on the lot, or a certification of no record) and to the Municipal Assessor (tax declarations on the buildings), so the returns are in before 2 December; and (c) have the judgment reserve to the owners the Article 1678 option for anything built before the deed, with no right of retention in any case?

**A8. The subpoena request (Annex 3).** I have drafted, for your signature, a single Request for Issuance of Subpoenas Duces Tecum and Ad Testificandum under Rule 21 and Section 5 of the Judicial Affidavit Rule, addressed to ten custodians and returnable on **December 2, 2026**: the Register of Deeds (Primary Entry Book for Entries 2021003235 and 2021003236, the complete entry files including the 15 March 2017 Partition-Subdivision Agreement, and the surrender record of the 2017 duplicate); the Clerk of Court (Atty. Asis's and Atty. Belen's notarial register entries and duplicate originals, the Spec. Proc. 2156 record, the Civil Case 8563 record); DENR Region V and Geodetic Engineer Mangiga (the PSD-E2020005406 file); the Building Official (permits or a certification of no record); the Municipal Assessor (ARPs 00246, 00247, 00274, 00276 and the declarations on the buildings); BIR RDO 64 (both eCAR dockets); the Provincial Treasurer (OR 0585696 and the penalty computation); the Provincial Prosecutor (the 2020 record with the 11 February 2020 counsel's letter); the Fire Marshal, CANORECO and the barangay; and COMELEC and the SB Secretary. Each item is described with particularity and carries a relevance sentence. Because the court records timely compliance and the returns must be in before our last two settings, could the request be announced on October 14 and filed by October 21? Your roll, PTR, IBP and MCLE particulars, the date and the service explanation are left blank for you.
